role: Fresh independent read-only reviewer; no artifact modifications.
task: Assess repaired checker and fixed offer-driver evidence. Return ready_for_offline_gate, findings, limitations. A detected genuine DUT violation does not imply a bad checker/testbench; separate specification violation, checker false positive, driver error and unresolved attribution. Do not authorize B/C automatically; final reachability/prompt/hash freeze is separate.

specification.scope: Original WBXBAR public bus boundary, revision 2e8d3bc2d26ddc33d1881022a2a2b9d3f0c16b9b. Two masters, two slaves. No internal state or submodule observation.

authority.representation: Maintainer paraphrase checked against PDF pages 31–38; not a new protocol specification.

requirements.summary: Reset takes effect on rising clock edges. Hold reset for at least one complete cycle. Master CYC and STB are inactive during reset; other master payload values are unspecified.
CYC qualifies bus activity and spans a transfer cycle. Without CYC, slave request signals are inactive. System reset remains effective.

Pipelined acceptance requires CYC and STB high and STALL low. WE distinguishes writes from reads. New requests need not wait for earlier acknowledgments. ACK can occur while STB is low. Successful transactions retire with acknowledgments; read data is meaningful with ACK.
ERR reports failure; the base protocol leaves the master reaction unspecified. ACK, ERR and RTY cannot coincide. Payload belongs to a strobed request. This interface has no RTY signal.

excerpts.text:
188: - [WBXBAR](rtl/wbxbar.v) is a fully function N master to M slave Wishbone
189:   [crossbar](https://zipcpu.com/blog/2019/07/17/crossbar.html).  Unlike my
190:   Unlike my [earlier WB interconnects](https://zipcpu.com/blog/2017/06/22/simple-wb-interconnect.html), this one guarantees that the
191:   ACK responses won't get crossed, and that misbehaving slave accesses will
192:   be timed out.  The core also has options for checking for starvation
193:   (where a master's request is not granted in a particular period of time),
194:   double-buffering all outputs (i.e. with [skid
195:   buffers](https://zipcpu.com/blog/2019/05/22/skidbuffer.html), and forcing idle
196:   channel values to zero in order to reduce power.

7: // Purpose:	A Configurable wishbone cross-bar interconnect, conforming
8: //		to the WB-B4 pipeline specification, as described on the
9: //	ZipCPU blog.
10: //
11: // Performance:
12: //	Throughput: One transaction per clock
13: //	Latency: One clock to get access to an unused channel, another to
14: //	place the results on the slave bus, and another to return, or a minimum
15: //	of three clocks.
16: //
17: // Usage: To use, you'll need to set NM and NS to the number of masters
18: //	(input ports) and the number of slaves respectively.  You'll then
19: //	want to set the addresses for the slaves in the SLAVE_ADDR array,
20: //	together with the SLAVE_MASK array indicating which SLAVE_ADDRs
21: //	are valid.  Address and data widths should be adjusted at the same
22: //	time.
23: //
24: //	Voila, you are now set up!
25: //
26: //	Now let's fine tune this:
27: //
28: //	LGMAXBURST can be set to control the maximum number of outstanding
29: //	transactions.  An LGMAXBURST of 6 will allow 63 outstanding
30: //	transactions.
31: //
32: //	OPT_TIMEOUT, if set to a non-zero value, is a number of clock periods
33: //	to wait for a slave to respond.  Should the timeout expire and the
34: //	slave not respond, a bus error will be returned and the slave will
35: //	be issued a bus abort signal (CYC will be dropped).
36: //
37: //	OPT_STARVATION_TIMEOUT, if set, applies the OPT_TIMEOUT counter to
38: //	how long a particular master waits for arbitration.  If the master is
39: //	"starved", a bus error will be returned.

authority.representation: Prose-only intent paraphrase; no implementation examples, expressions or internal signal names included. Older design article is supplementary, not exact-cycle authority.

requirements.location: What is a Crossbar?; Returning data, paragraphs on nonexistent addresses and abort
requirements.summary: A crossbar connects masters to slaves without mixing their responses. A request outside every configured address range should return an error. A master may end its cycle to abort outstanding work; completed data must not later be attributed to a new transaction. The article motivates aborting a cycle after an error. Exact buffering, arbitration and timeout edge counts require explicit documentation rather than assumptions.

interface.packing: Port 0 occupies the least-significant slice. Each address is an 8-bit bus address, each data value 32 bits, each select 4 bits. No implicit byte-address shifting.
interface.address_configuration: Slave0: (addr & 0xf0)==0x00; slave1: (addr & 0xf0)==0x10. Other addresses match neither slave. This is public parameter decoding, not stimulus guidance.
interface.directions: i_m* are external master inputs; o_m* are DUT responses. o_s* are DUT requests to external slaves; i_s* are external slave responses. i_clk is the common clock.
interface.rows: [{cycle:int, pre:{all listed inputs and outputs}, post:{all listed outputs}}]; integers of declared width. None may represent undefined inactive payload, never a valid active control/data value.
interface.sampling: Inputs change while clock low. Pre sampled at +4ns, rising edge at +5ns, post at +9ns, falling edge at +10ns. One row is one physical cycle. Initial trace has two reset cycles followed by quiescence. No extra hidden clock edges.
interface.boundary: Checker consumes actual public-pin observations, not model offers or driver queue ledgers. Drivers may queue offers and hold pins through acceptance. Do not trust driver internal accounting as functional truth.
interface.environment_contract: External masters obey pipelined acceptance, holding pending request payload through backpressure except explicit cycle abort/reset. External slaves respond in acceptance order, may wait, and do not generate unsolicited responses. Slave work is canceled on cycle withdrawal/reset. Record violations separately from DUT faults. Exact future JSON offer fields are irrelevant to the pin-based checker.

requested_obligations: mapped request routing and payload/byte-mask preservation
response order, destination and read-data preservation across concurrent masters
no invented/duplicated successful transaction, reset and abort epoch separation
unmapped/slave-error response and subsequent restart; timeout scope explicitly justified
specification.isolation: No executable DUT RTL, prior checker, calibrated traces, source targets, coverage results, semantic equivalences or model outcomes.

previous_review.summary: The checker is structurally sound for routing, payload and SEL preservation, per-master ordering, read data, slave-ERR propagation and pending accounting. Its pin-level controls are mostly legal and isolate real requirements. One blocking gap remains. Timeout/starvation ERR is accepted unconditionally for any mapped request without a slave ACK, and the trace still gets a scoped_pass. A DUT that answers every mapped request with an immediate ERR, never forwarding, would therefore pass. This verdict covers checker adequacy only. It is not a live-run freeze, does not cover the pending driver, and is not a formal proof.

findings.detail: The control negative/early_unexplained_error returns scoped_pass. It is a mapped request on an idle fabric with a single master, so there is no contention. ERR arrives one cycle after acceptance, with no slave ERR. The response branch labels any non-sacked entry 'timeout_or_starvation_err' with no eligibility condition. The wbxbar.v header (lines 32-39) ties the bus error to OPT_TIMEOUT: a slave failing to respond within a number of clock periods (16 here), or a master waiting for arbitration that long under OPT_STARVATION_TIMEOUT. The crossbar article ties ERR to nonexistent addresses. No documented mechanism explains a mapped-address ERR after one cycle with no slave ERR and no competing master. The control is therefore justified. Enforcing it does not require an exact implementation counter. Contract.md and P9 do disclose the exclusion. However, the scoped_pass label overstates coverage of the 'no invented response' and 'unmapped/slave-error/timeout scope justified' obligations.
findings.recommended_disposition: Pick one of two minimal changes and re-run the controls. (a) Downgrade any timeout_or_starvation_err retirement to an unresolved item, so the trace can never reach scoped_pass. (b) Fail ERR on a mapped request with no slave ERR when two conditions hold: the request has waited well under OPT_TIMEOUT cycles since acceptance, and the other master held no CYC during that time. Option (b) is a conservative lower bound, not an exact counter. Do not alter the control.

findings.detail: negative/stale_after_reset injects o_mack while i_mcyc=0, and the checker ignores it per the contract. Under WB B4 3.1.2 (rules 3.25/3.30), CYC qualifies bus activity, so an unqualified response while CYC is low is not attributable to any transaction. Ignoring it is an acceptable declared exclusion, and the control should not be counted as an expected detection. The harmful case is a stale ACK landing on a new accepted transaction. That case is detected by negative/stale_into_new_epoch, which reports a 'response' failure at cycle 16 and an invented_response at cycle 20.
findings.recommended_disposition: Reclassify the control as a declared-exclusion or informational case. Optionally emit a descriptive note for responses while CYC is low. No change to the checker's functional verdict is required.

findings.detail: Identical concurrent heads set amb=True and append an unresolved entry before anything else. While amb is set, invented, unsolicited and retirement checks are skipped, and completion events are suppressed. The unresolved entry persists, so the verdict cannot reach scoped_pass. Assumption violations still dominate. One residual path remains: a decode or timeout ERR before ambiguity arises still passes, because of F1.

A reset row clears both queues and checks post-edge o_scyc/o_sstb. A stale slave ACK after reset is classified as an environment violation, which matches the contract's cancellation rule. When a master drops CYC, its entries are marked aborted. A later slave response to aborted work is discarded as an orphan and cannot retire new work. Gaps: o_mack/o_merr are not checked inactive after the reset edge. The 'reset held for at least one full cycle' rule is not checked. The checker does not require the DUT to eventually withdraw o_scyc after a master abort or timeout. These are acceptable only as documented exclusions.

Accepts are appended before responses are popped, so an accept and an earlier response on the same edge retire the correct oldest entry; positive/accept_and_return confirms this. A slave ACK on its own acceptance edge, or a master ACK on the acceptance edge with an empty queue, is attributed to the brand-new entry. On the master side this correctly fails, because the entry state is 'new'. On the slave side a zero-latency slave would be credited rather than flagged. That is an environment-side looseness, not a DUT false negative.

findings.topic: Write data compared under masked bytes
findings.detail: Full 32-bit write data is compared even when SEL bytes are deasserted. WB B4 does not require masked byte lanes to be preserved. This is low risk for this DUT configuration, but it could produce a spec-unsupported failure.
findings.recommended_disposition: Document this as a stricter-than-spec choice, or compare only the SEL-enabled lanes.

findings.detail: Events inside any failure or assumption window are dropped, and all events are dropped if a failure has no cycle. Completion events require a slave ACK attributed to the same entry. Remaining concern: the 'timeout_or_starvation_err' events label unexplained errors as legitimate mechanisms (see F1). Reset events are purely descriptive.

The positive traces respect pipelined acceptance and response-order assumptions. Each single-fault negative changes one public-pin aspect relative to a clean baseline. Some negatives produce two failures (for example routing_payload plus a cascaded response failure), which is acceptable. invalid/master_changes_stalled_payload correctly yields input_or_scope_invalid. The 44 clean DUT traces are observations, not golden references.

Controls still needed: (1) A master CYC abort with forwarded work outstanding, followed by a late slave ACK and then a new transaction on the same master, checking the orphan is not credited. (2) A DUT-side stalled slave request that changes payload or drops STB (P8 negative). (3) o_mack and o_merr coinciding. (4) An identical-request ambiguity case, expecting unresolved. (5) A decode-error request interleaved between mapped requests on one master, checking ordering. (6) A slave ERR mid-burst followed by further accepted requests and restart. (7) Contention from two masters to one slave, including a starvation-window case. (8) A master ACK/ERR asserted during or immediately after reset. (9) A partial-SEL write with differing masked bytes (F6). (10) Pending items at batch end with both master-side and slave-side obligations.

limitations: This is a read-only review of the supplied packet; no code was executed and no artifacts were modified.
This is not a formal proof. Ten clean hand positives and 44 clean DUT traces do not establish whole-IP correctness, target reachability, or live B/C comparability.
Exact arbitration, pipeline and timeout latencies are not established by the cited authority. Any timing bound proposed in F1 is a conservative lower bound, not an implementation counter.
The final experimental driver is pending and is out of scope. Readiness here concerns the checker only.
Only 8 of the 44 DUT traces were shown in full. The others were assessed through their reported diagnostics.

candidate.selftest.py:
KEYS=['i_reset','i_mcyc','i_mstb','i_mwe','i_maddr','i_mdata','i_msel','i_sstall','i_sack','i_sdata','i_serr','o_mstall','o_mack','o_mdata','o_merr','o_scyc','o_sstb','o_swe','o_saddr','o_sdata','o_ssel']

def _row(c,**kw):
    pre={k:0 for k in KEYS}
    pre.update(kw)
    post={k:0 for k in KEYS if k.startswith('o_')}
    return {'cycle':c,'pre':pre,'post':post}

def _base():
    return [_row(0,i_reset=1),_row(1,i_reset=1)]

def _wr(sd=0xAB,sa=0x05,ss=0,sel=0xF):
    rows=_base()
    rows.append(_row(2,i_mcyc=1,i_mstb=1,i_mwe=1,i_maddr=0x05,i_mdata=0xAB,i_msel=sel))
    rows.append(_row(3,i_mcyc=1,o_scyc=1<<ss,o_sstb=1<<ss,o_swe=1<<ss,o_saddr=sa<<(8*ss),o_sdata=sd<<(32*ss),o_ssel=sel<<(4*ss)))
    rows.append(_row(4,i_mcyc=1,o_scyc=1<<ss,i_sack=1<<ss))
    rows.append(_row(5,i_mcyc=1,o_mack=1))
    rows.append(_row(6))
    return rows

def _rd(md=0x55):
    rows=_base()
    rows.append(_row(2,i_mcyc=2,i_mstb=2,i_maddr=0x12<<8,i_msel=0xF<<4))
    rows.append(_row(3,i_mcyc=2,o_scyc=2,o_sstb=2,o_saddr=0x12<<8,o_ssel=0xF<<4))
    rows.append(_row(4,i_mcyc=2,o_scyc=2,i_sack=2,i_sdata=0x55<<32))
    rows.append(_row(5,i_mcyc=2,o_mack=2,o_mdata=md<<32))
    rows.append(_row(6))
    return rows

def _unm(ack=False):
    rows=_base()
    rows.append(_row(2,i_mcyc=1,i_mstb=1,i_maddr=0x40,i_msel=0xF))
    rows.append(_row(3,i_mcyc=1))
    if ack:
        rows.append(_row(4,i_mcyc=1,o_mack=1))
    else:
        rows.append(_row(4,i_mcyc=1,o_merr=1))
    rows.append(_row(5))
    return rows

def _shift(rows,off):
    return [{'cycle':r['cycle']+off,'pre':r['pre'],'post':r['post']} for r in rows]

def _early_err():
    rows=_base()
    rows.append(_row(2,i_mcyc=1,i_mstb=1,i_maddr=0x05,i_msel=0xF))
    rows.append(_row(3,i_mcyc=1,o_merr=1))
    rows.append(_row(4))
    return rows

def _early_err_then_reset():
    return _early_err()+[_row(5,i_reset=1)]+_shift(_wr()[2:],4)

def _slave_err():
    rows=_base()
    rows.append(_row(2,i_mcyc=1,i_mstb=1,i_maddr=0x05,i_msel=0xF))
    rows.append(_row(3,i_mcyc=1,o_scyc=1,o_sstb=1,o_saddr=0x05,o_ssel=0xF))
    rows.append(_row(4,i_mcyc=1,o_scyc=1,i_serr=1))
    rows.append(_row(5,i_mcyc=1,o_merr=1))
    rows.append(_row(6))
    return rows

def run(check_rows):
    tests=[
        ('write_positive',_wr(),'scoped_pass'),
        ('write_payload_fault',_wr(sd=0xAC),'dut_violation'),
        ('write_misroute_fault',_wr(ss=1),'dut_violation'),
        ('read_positive',_rd(),'scoped_pass'),
        ('read_data_fault',_rd(md=0x56),'dut_violation'),
        ('unmapped_err_positive',_unm(),'scoped_pass'),
        ('unmapped_ack_fault',_unm(ack=True),'dut_violation'),
        ('invented_ack_fault',_base()+[_row(2,i_mcyc=1,o_mack=1),_row(3)],'dut_violation'),
        ('incomplete_unresolved',_wr()[:4],'unresolved'),
        ('early_unexplained_err_unresolved',_early_err(),'unresolved'),
        ('unexplained_err_persists_after_reset',_early_err_then_reset(),'unresolved'),
        ('slave_err_positive',_slave_err(),'scoped_pass'),
        ('masked_lane_write_positive',_wr(sd=0x5500AB,sel=0x1),'scoped_pass'),
        ('enabled_lane_write_fault',_wr(sd=0xAC,sel=0x1),'dut_violation'),
        ('unsolicited_slave_ack_env',_base()+[_row(2,o_scyc=1,i_sack=1),_row(3)],'input_or_scope_invalid'),
    ]
    out=[]
    for n,r,exp in tests:
        try:
            ok=check_rows(r)['verdict']==exp
        except Exception:
            ok=False
        out.append({'name':n,'pass':ok})
    return out
candidate.contract.md:
# WBXBAR spec checker contract

**Scope:** public pins of wbxbar rev 2e8d3bc2, NM=2, NS=2, AW=8, DW=32, with the packet's decode. Only pre-edge values define transfers; post values are used only for post-reset output checks. Reset is synchronous. The trace must start with reset and have contiguous cycles.

**Checked:**
- routing
- payload and SEL preservation (write data compared only on SEL-enabled byte lanes; address, WE, SEL compared fully)
- per-master in-order retirement
- ACK only after the matching slave ACK
- read-data equality with slave-returned data
- decode ERR for unmapped addresses
- slave ERR propagation
- abort/reset/CYC-drop epoch separation
- stalled-request hold and basic handshake legality

**Environment violations:** these are reported separately and yield input_or_scope_invalid. They include:
- master hold or STB-without-CYC
- unsolicited slave responses
- undefined active payload
- CYC/STB high during reset

**Limitations:**
- Exact arbitration, pipeline and timeout latencies are not checked. A master ERR on a mapped request with no matching slave ERR is recorded as unresolved (unexplained_mapped_err, with accept/ERR cycles); it is never scoped_pass and is not labeled timeout/starvation. It persists across later reset/restart in the same batch.
- Responses while master CYC is low are ignored (not attributable per WB B4 3.1.2); stale responses landing on new work are checked.
- Not checked: o_mack/o_merr inactive after reset, minimum reset duration, eventual o_scyc withdrawal after abort/timeout (liveness).
- Identical concurrent requests from both masters make ownership ambiguous. Functional checks are then suspended until reset and reported as unresolved.
- Pending work at trace end yields unresolved.
- Events are descriptive and are dropped if any failure falls in their window.
- The per-master forwarding order assumption is derived from the no-crossed-ACK claim.
- The selftests are minimal and are not certification.

"""Protocol-safe offer driver; no expected DUT outputs or coverage targeting.

Separate from the frozen ordinary-screen driver: supports pending batches and
mandatory low-CYC gap after errors, keeping queued unaccepted offers for restart.
"""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
from probe_wbxbar_ordinary import FIELDS, seed, action, cases, driver as ordinary_driver, comparable
from probe_wbxbar_ordinary import validate as ordinary_validate
from prepare_wbxbar_checker_role import verify_scope
from run_midterm_fixed import ROOT, sha, invoke
from inventory_natural_coverage import load_all
from preflight_spi_host import identity

BASE = ROOT / 'results/wbxbar_conditional_20261104/screen-v2'


def validate(actions):
    ordinary_validate(actions)
    if any(a['rst'] and a['offer'] for a in actions):
        raise ValueError('Offers during reset are not supported')


def driver(candidate, ports):
    text, inputs, outputs = ordinary_driver(candidate, ports)
    replacements = [
        ('integer fd,nread,cycle,m,head[0:1]', 'integer cooldown[0:1];\ninteger fd,nread,cycle,m,head[0:1]'),
        ('returned[m]=0;', 'returned[m]=0;cooldown[m]=0;'),
        ('i_mcyc[m]=!r_rst &&', 'i_mcyc[m]=!r_rst && cooldown[m]==0 &&'),
        ('i_mstb[m]=!r_rst &&', 'i_mstb[m]=!r_rst && cooldown[m]==0 &&'),
        ('  if(r_rst) begin previous_slave=0;response_data=0;end',
         '  for(m=0;m<2;m=m+1) if(cooldown[m]>0) cooldown[m]=cooldown[m]-1;\n  if(r_rst) begin previous_slave=0;response_data=0;end'),
        ('   if(pending[m]<0) $fatal(1,"orphan master response");',
         '   if(pending[m]<0) begin $display("DUT_DIAGNOSTIC orphan_response cycle=%0d master=%0d",cycle,m);pending[m]=0;end\n'
         '   if(pre_response[m] && o_merr[m]) begin pending[m]=0;cooldown[m]=1;end'),
        ('for(m=0;m<2;m=m+1) if(head[m]!=tail[m] || pending[m]!=0) $fatal(1,"ordinary delivery incomplete");',
         'for(m=0;m<2;m=m+1) $display("PENDING %0d %0d %0d",m,tail[m]-head[m],pending[m]);')]
    # Error must use the sampled PRE error, not the next POST output.
    replacements += [
        ('reg [1:0] previous_slave,pre_master,pre_response,pre_slave;', 'reg [1:0] previous_slave,pre_master,pre_response,pre_slave,pre_error;'),
        ('  pre_response=i_mcyc & (o_mack | o_merr);', '  pre_response=i_mcyc & (o_mack | o_merr);pre_error=i_mcyc & o_merr;'),
        ('if(pre_response[m] && o_merr[m])', 'if(pre_error[m])')]
    for before, after in replacements:
        expected = 2 if before == 'returned[m]=0;' else 1
        if text.count(before) != expected: raise ValueError('Ordinary template drift: ' + before)
        text = text.replace(before, after)
    return text, inputs, outputs


def parse(log, actions, inputs, outputs):
    records, ledgers = {}, {}
    for line in log.splitlines():
        fields = line.split()
        if not fields: continue
        if fields[0] == 'QUEUE':
            ledgers[int(fields[1]), int(fields[2])] = list(map(int, fields[3:])); continue
        if fields[0] not in ('PRE','POST'): continue
        names = inputs + outputs if fields[0] == 'PRE' else outputs
        if len(fields) != len(names)+2: raise ValueError('Trace field count')
        phase = fields[0].lower(); cycle = int(fields[1])
        if phase in records.setdefault(cycle, {}): raise ValueError('Duplicate trace row')
        records[cycle][phase] = {n: None if any(c in v.lower() for c in 'xz') else int(v,16) for n,v in zip(names, fields[2:])}
    if list(records) != list(range(len(actions))) or len(ledgers) != 2*len(actions):
        raise ValueError('Incomplete trace')
    queues = [[],[]]; sent = [0,0]; returned = [0,0]; pending = [0,0]; cooldown = [0,0]
    previous_slave = 0; response_data = 0; trace = []; diagnostics = []
    totals = dict.fromkeys(['offers','accepted','responses','reset_discarded_queued','reset_discarded_accepted','error_aborted_accepted'],0)
    for cycle, a in enumerate(actions):
        pre, post = records[cycle]['pre'], records[cycle]['post']
        want = dict.fromkeys(inputs,0); want['i_reset'] = a['rst']
        if a['rst']:
            totals['reset_discarded_queued'] += sum(map(len,queues)); totals['reset_discarded_accepted'] += sum(pending)
            queues=[[],[]];sent=[0,0];returned=[0,0];pending=[0,0];cooldown=[0,0];previous_slave=0;response_data=0
        for m in (0,1):
            if not a['rst'] and a['offer'] >> m & 1:
                queues[m].append(tuple(a[k]>>shift & ((1<<width)-1) for k,shift,width in
                    [('addr',8*m,8),('data',32*m,32),('we',m,1),('sel',4*m,4)]))
                totals['offers'] += 1
            active = not a['rst'] and cooldown[m] == 0
            want['i_mcyc'] |= int(active and bool(queues[m] or pending[m])) << m
            want['i_mstb'] |= int(active and bool(queues[m])) << m
            if want['i_mstb'] >> m & 1:
                for key,value,shift in zip(('i_maddr','i_mdata','i_mwe','i_msel'),queues[m][0],(8*m,32*m,m,4*m)):
                    want[key] |= value << shift
            cooldown[m] = max(0,cooldown[m]-1)
        scyc = pre['o_scyc'] or 0
        want.update(i_sack=previous_slave & ~a['slave_error'] & scyc & (0 if a['rst'] else 3),
                    i_serr=previous_slave & a['slave_error'] & scyc & (0 if a['rst'] else 3), i_sdata=response_data)
        if any(pre[k] != v for k,v in want.items()):
            raise ValueError('JSON/pin mismatch at cycle ' + str(cycle))
        for m in (0,1):
            accept = bool(want['i_mcyc']>>m&1 and want['i_mstb']>>m&1 and not pre['o_mstall']>>m&1)
            response = bool(want['i_mcyc']>>m&1 and (pre['o_mack']|pre['o_merr'])>>m&1)
            error = bool(want['i_mcyc']>>m&1 and pre['o_merr']>>m&1)
            if accept:queues[m].pop(0);sent[m]+=1;totals['accepted']+=1
            if response:returned[m]+=1;totals['responses']+=1
            pending[m] += int(accept)-int(response)
            if pending[m] < 0:
                diagnostics.append({'cycle':cycle,'master':m,'kind':'orphan_response'});pending[m]=0
            if error:
                totals['error_aborted_accepted'] += pending[m];pending[m]=0;cooldown[m]=1
            h,t,p,ac,ret = ledgers[cycle,m]
            if (h,t-h,p,ac,ret) != (sent[m],len(queues[m]),pending[m],sent[m],returned[m]):
                raise ValueError('Transport ledger mismatch')
        previous_slave = 0 if a['rst'] else pre['o_scyc'] & pre['o_sstb']
        response_data = sum((0xa55a0000 | ((pre['o_saddr'] or 0)>>(8*m)&255))<<(32*m) for m in (0,1))
        trace.append({'cycle':cycle,'pre':pre,'post':post})
    totals.update(queued=sum(map(len,queues)),outstanding=sum(pending),diagnostics=diagnostics,
                  delivery_complete=not any(queues) and not any(pending),cycles=len(actions))
    return trace, totals
driver.source_scope: Exact generator and Python transport parser. Build and case-generation helpers omitted; standalone compiled SV and evidence are supplied.
driver.boundary: Same original public ports/parameters/denominator. One action is one physical cycle. Per-master offer queues; hold STB/payload until sampled acceptance. CYC persists for outstanding work. On sampled ERR discard remaining accepted work and keep unaccepted offers, with one counted low-CYC gap. Reset discards pending/queued work. No hidden drains. Cumulative-prefix replay preserves pins.
driver.unit_checks: Six tests pass: pending prefix remains incomplete, aborted/reset requests not counted as responses, counted CYC gap, mutated abort input rejected, reset+offer rejected, exact prefix pin replay.

traces.encoding: first is complete vector; each [repeat, [[index,value],...]] applies updates repeat times, one new cycle each time. Other values persist. For deltas, decode base then truncate to length, apply listed pre/post field updates at index. Empty action is packing-only. Every vector/delta roundtrip checked.
traces.disclosure: All 38 independent hand controls and 6 selected driver traces included losslessly. Diagnostics supplied for all 44 old and all 48 new DUT observations; unshown traces are not independently reread by this reviewer.

8: //		to the WB-B4 pipeline specification, as described on the
9: //	ZipCPU blog.
10: //
11: // Performance:
12: //	Throughput: One transaction per clock
13: //	Latency: One clock to get access to an unused channel, another to
14: //	place the results on the slave bus, and another to return, or a minimum
15: //	of three clocks.
16: //
17: // Usage: To use, you'll need to set NM and NS to the number of masters
18: //	(input ports) and the number of slaves respectively.  You'll then
19: //	want to set the addresses for the slaves in the SLAVE_ADDR array,
20: //	together with the SLAVE_MASK array indicating which SLAVE_ADDRs
21: //	are valid.  Address and data widths should be adjusted at the same
22: //	time.
23: //
24: //	Voila, you are now set up!
25: //
26: //	Now let's fine tune this:
27: //
28: //	LGMAXBURST can be set to control the maximum number of outstanding
29: //	transactions.  An LGMAXBURST of 6 will allow 63 outstanding
30: //	transactions.
31: //
32: //	OPT_TIMEOUT, if set to a non-zero value, is a number of clock periods
33: //	to wait for a slave to respond.  Should the timeout expire and the
34: //	slave not respond, a bus error will be returned and the slave will
35: //	be issued a bus abort signal (CYC will be dropped).
36: //
37: //	OPT_STARVATION_TIMEOUT, if set, applies the OPT_TIMEOUT counter to
38: //	how long a particular master waits for arbitration.  If the master is

41: //	OPT_DBLBUFFER is used to increase clock speed by registering all
42: //	outputs.
43: //
